Horace Walpole, The Castle of Otranto, edited by Henry Morley.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/horace-walpole/the-castle-of-otranto

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Horace Walpole, the author, died 1797.
- Henry Morley, the editor and writer of the introduction, died 1894.

First publication of the text used: 1764 (SE colophon: 'The Castle of Otranto was published in 1764 by Horace Walpole'; Wikipedia, 'The Castle of Otranto': publication date 24 December 1764, publication place England).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1764, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom, England): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1894, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1965.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
